Q: View the change history of a file using Git versioning A:

For a graphical view, use gitk:

gitk [filename]

To follow the file across file renames:

gitk --follow [filename]

For a console view, maybe because you SSH into a head-less server, run:

git blame-log <filename>

However, first ensure blame-log command exists, by at least once running:

# Virables: raw=unchanged-line, c=clean, B=Buffer,
git config --global alias.blame-log "! cd -- \"\${GIT_PREFIX:-.}\" && \
( if git grep -qI \".\" \"\$1\"; then \
    git log --oneline --color=always -L 1,\${2:-}:\"\$1\" | awk ' \
    { s=\$0; gsub(/\\033\\[[0-9;]*[mK]/, \"\", s) } \
    s~/^(diff|---|\\+\\+\+)/{next} \
    s~/^@@/{l=1;p=9;bi=0;cm=0;cp=0;next} s!~/^[-+ ]/{print;l=1;p=9;bi=0;cm=0;cp=0;next} \
    /^ /{ cm=0;cp=0; if(p<3){print;p++}else{b[bi%3]=\$0; bl[bi%3]=l; bi++} l++; next } \
    { if(p>=3){ n=(bi<3?bi:3); st=(bi<3?0:bi%3); print \"\\033[36mLine \"(n?bl[st]:l)\":\\033[m\"; for(k=0;k<n;k++)print b[(st+k)%3] } \
      p=0; if(s~/^-/){cm++;if(cm<=12)print;else if(cm==13)print\"...\"} else{cp++;if(cp<=12)print;else if(cp==13)print\"...\";l++} }'; \
else \
    echo \"Detected binary file, hence not showing lines-changed.\"
    git log --oneline --color=always \"\$1\";
fi ) | less -RX #"

Note that blame-log is intentionally limited to showing few lines per change-range, for example, to skip package-lock.json faster.

Q: Update Pandas Series with Multiindex A:

You can use pd.IndexSlice to use multi-index slicing:

i_lvl = s1_ik.index.get_level_values('i')
k_lvl = s1_ik.index.get_level_values('k')
idx = pd.IndexSlice[i_lvl, j, k_lvl]

s0_ijk.loc[idx] = s1_ik

Output:

>>> s0_ijk
i  j  k
0  0  0    1
      1    1
      2    1
   1  0    0
      1    0
      2    0
dtype: int64

Q: Plotting mplot3d / axes3D xyz surface plot with log scale? A:

This has been fixed with the merge of https://github.com/matplotlib/matplotlib/pull/30980 and will be available in matplotlib 3.11.

Setting 3D axes to log, symlog, or any other scale transform will work with the same command as in 2D:

ax.set_xscale('log')

Q: TypeError: The "original" argument must be of type Function A:

The issue is with the require. "@tensorflow/tfjs-node" exports multiple things(possibly), so the export inside this module would be something like 

module.exports = {
    firstThing,
    secondThing, ...
}

So, tf in your code is an object, and not a function. So, you should use named import like this,

const {tf} = require('@tensorflow/tfjs-node')

So, you are getting an error when invoking tf. I have not worked with this package, but this seems like the cause for error. If it doesn't fix the issue, please add the line that is throwing the error.

Q: Slow HikariDataSource.getConnection() on slow on low traffic, fast on big traffic A:

You can set idleTimeout when minimumIdle is defined as less than maximumPoolSize

⌚idleTimeout This property controls the maximum amount of time that a connection is allowed to sit idle in the pool. This setting only applies when minimumIdle is defined to be less than maximumPoolSize. Idle connections will not be retired once the pool reaches minimumIdle connections.
